content.title: About
content.content: Lactose‑free reduced‑fat milk (2%) is pasteurized cow’s milk that has had most of its lactose removed and the fat content lowered to 2 %. It retains the majority of the nutrients found in regular milk while being easier to digest for those with lactose intolerance and suitable for low‑fat diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lactose is removed using lactase enzymes or filtration, making the product safe for most people with lactose intolerance.
Reduced‑fat milk is popular in diet and sports nutrition because of its lower calorie content.
At 2 % fat, the milk still provides fat‑soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K, though in smaller amounts than whole milk.
In some countries, lactose‑free milk is classified as a separate food category with specific labeling regulations.
The lactose‑removal process preserves the natural taste of milk, unlike many plant‑based alternatives.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Milk is rich in calcium and vitamin D, which are essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: A serving provides about 7 g of complete milk protein, important for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Easy to digest for lactose‑intolerant individuals
items.content: Removing lactose allows those with intolerance to enjoy milk’s nutrients without discomfort.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The 2 % fat content makes the product less caloric, helping with weight management while retaining nutritional value.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12) support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to this milk regardless of lactose content.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although lactose is removed, some brands add sweeteners; check the label if you monitor sugar intake.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Certain products are fortified with extra vitamins or minerals; those with sensitivities should read the ingredient list.

items.title: Storage safety
items.content: After opening, keep the milk refrigerated and consume within 5–7 days to prevent microbial spoilage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lactose‑free reduced‑fat milk can be enjoyed plain, added to cereals, smoothies, coffee, baked goods, and sauces. It pairs well with fruit, berries, and grains and serves as a base for low‑fat desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the milk in the refrigerator at 1–4 °C. Keep the container tightly sealed after opening. Discard if it develops a sour smell, off‑taste, or changes in texture.
